candidate.name: ACTH, corticosteroids and phenobarbital-containing regimens (class level)

disease_assertion.endpoint: clinical response as the curation records it ('Yes' undefined; West syndrome frequent in the cohort)

context.disease_id: WWOX-related epilepsy, heterogeneous curation of more than 21 reports (West syndrome frequent)
context.genotype: not carried by the source row (heterogeneous reports; allele classes not stated)

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: clinical cessation of epileptic spasms, if and only if a comparator separates a WWOX-genotype response from ordinary West-syndrome pharmacology
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: none for the gene: six explicit responders in a per-patient supplement column of one curation, 'Yes' undefined, no control arm, dosing, duration or standardised follow-up
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: heterogeneous primary reports; West syndrome and hypsarrhythmia are frequent in this cohort and hormonal therapy is standard care for infantile spasms generally

cellular_context.limits: no candidate, so no target-expression statement is made

p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Class level only; no named product, formulation or regimen.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Human WWOX-DEE reports, more than 21 heterogeneous primary reports tabulated in one curation.
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Already used. Not a new idea.
p4_roadmap_fields.known_roads_state: Partial, confounded by West-syndrome pharmacology (known-roads note 2.7); visible only in the supplement while the running text calls the regimens flatly not effective.
p4_roadmap_fields.expected_contribution: Symptom, to be verified; unseparated from standard care.
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: Known-roads note 2.7; CLAIM 001 (hormonal therapy as a VABAM co-factor in non-WWOX cohorts).
p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Six explicit responders against an undefined response and no comparator.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: In a matched non-WWOX West-syndrome series, what fraction responds to hormonal therapy, and how many WWOX responders would that fraction already explain?
p4_roadmap_fields.status: ASTENSIONE. Missing datum: a defined response and a matched West-syndrome base rate.
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Keeps a visible-but-confounded observation from being read as a WWOX-specific road.

not_known: genotype class of the six explicit responders (not carried by the source row)

evaluation_frame.source: repurposing_10h_scientist-d_20261021.md, 'The answer in one page', DESIGN TABLE A and B. INFERENZA built from precedents that are all NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; the manifests of that note were blind-audited on 2026-10-22 (207 of 215 triples supported, eight repaired; the repairs are unaudited).
a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); no measurement of the scatter of an untreated interval in WOREE is established here (the repository's series have one timepoint per patient; no wider search was run)
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter

the word protection: in the human precedents read for this frame none measured the preservation of a function that would otherwise have been lost; the repository's mouse rescue studies are outside this frame and the scope of 'this corpus' is not defined, so no wider negative is established here

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.
